q2_forgetting.curator_notes: Ranked by (how overdue) x (whether the counterparty has chased) x (consequence); the covenant compliance certificate now outranks the board-deck slide since its blocking condition cleared Jul 24 and it is by far the more stale of the two. Every item is attested by owner-authored promise language in SENT or DRAFT mail with no closing message anywhere in the mailbox. The conditional promise to Frank about the amendment itself is excluded (moved to must_not_include): the Third Amendment was signed by all parties on Aug 12, so that commitment is discharged, not forgotten — only the residual 'I'll keep you posted either way' status update would remain, and it is too thin to carry its own item. The revenue-rec memo item is narrowed to the still-open Jul 29 update; the base memo was delivered Jul 25 and is not itself a forgetting. The lease-amortization half of the Pemberton PBC promise has been split out of q2-02 since it was re-dated and delegated to Miles (Aug 14) — it is tracked in Q4 as a wait, not a lapse. Ironforge's W-9 chase is likewise removed from here and belongs to Q4 (owner is waiting on the vendor, not forgetting her own promise). Hannah's retracted headcount commitment is deliberately excluded. The counter-proposal redlines are borderline because later messages imply the negotiation continued by phone. Audit fieldwork-start dates are stated inconsistently across the corpus (week of Sep 8 vs. Aug 11) — this set uses Aug 11 as it is the most specific and recent statement, but a reader should treat the exact date as soft.

q6_slipping_through_cracks.curator_notes: Ranked by consequence x invisibility x elapsed time. The Harborline phishing email now ranks first: it is the single most invisible item in the corpus (spam-foldered, unstarred, unflagged, and the only fraud message with zero tricky-tag annotation) riding directly on the live, high-dollar credit facility closing. It legitimately also appears in Q1 (as a lower, spam-mitigated hazard, finance-q1-12) — Q6 cares about its invisibility, Q1 about whether it needs looking at today; the spam-quarantine somewhat blunts today's urgency but does nothing to reduce how easily it would be missed if AP or Aditi ever checked the spam folder. Every other item passes both tests: a real dollar amount or stakeholder, plus a burial factor (bounce, bcc, attachment-only, quote-only, ambiguous owner, topic drift, auto-responder, off-thread personal address). Items the owner visibly engaged with — the unsent Ironforge draft, the missed rev-rec memo — are deliberately left in Q2 instead. The capex and expense-report items appear here as well as in Q1/Q3 because the burial, not the deadline, is what makes them dangerous.
